jobs.name: Brief - Morning
jobs.prompt:
Produce a polished Morning Brief.

The measured brief context (weather, infra scan, reminders, AI infra events) is injected above under the "===== BRIEF CONTEXT =====" header. Treat that as your ONLY source for weather, infra, and reminders. The AI infra events section additionally allows the bounded web step described under HARD RULES.

HARD RULES
- Weather: report only values present in the injected context. If it says WEATHER SOURCE UNAVAILABLE, write "outlook unavailable". Never invent or generalize a forecast.
- Infra: only call something down if the scan prints a red cross. Entries under "Known-inactive by design" are NOT issues and must not be reported as down.
- Do NOT claim whether work was completed, shipped, or not shipped. You have no source for that. Do not state or imply it either way.
- AI infra events: this section has a measured base and an optional web extension.
  BASE (always): every line under "UPCOMING (chronological)" in the injected AI INFRA EVENTS block is authoritative. Reproduce each one exactly - date, name, [vendor] tag, URL. Never drop, re-sort, or regroup these.
  WEB (additive only): two sources the scraper structurally cannot read, so fetch them with the web tools. Each has a strict filter - apply it or skip the source.
    (1) https://vllm.ai/events - take only items under "Upcoming & live", each of which shows an explicit month/day/year. Their dates are real; several may share one date, which is normal, not an error. Ignore "Loading events..." and the calendar-grid day counts.
    (2) https://www.brighttalk.com/topic/gpu - IMPORTANT: fetch this with an explicit large char_limit (40000). The page is ~28000 chars and the default limit truncates the MIDDLE, which is exactly where every upcoming session lives - without it you will see the head and tail only and wrongly conclude there are no upcoming events. When extracting, pass char_limit=40000 explicitly; do not rely on the default.
        This page is ~80% already-published recordings and MUST NOT be dumped into a forward-looking brief. Keep ONLY webinar links whose URL contains the literal substring "utm_content=upcoming"; every recording instead carries "utm_content=on-demand", and recordings are also marked "on-demand" or given as a relative age like "4 months ago". Ignore all of those. An entry with no explicit future date is not an event - drop it.
  Skip a source if its fetch fails: never retry more than once, never substitute a different site, and never fill a gap from memory or from a search-result summary.
  MERGE: output one chronologically sorted list, earliest first, base plus any web additions. Format each web addition exactly like a base line: "- <Day Mon DD> · <name> [<vendor>] - [<details>](<url>)" — markdown link, never a bare URL.
  HONESTY: an event you did not see on a page this run does not exist. Never infer, estimate, or recall an event from an earlier day. If a web source is unreachable, silently omit it - do not report the failure.
  If there is no UPCOMING block AND the web step yields nothing, write "event watch unavailable". Lines saying 'no events in window' or 'SOURCE UNAVAILABLE' are per-vendor status, not events: ignore them.
  Do not describe any event's content, speakers, or value; you cannot see it.
- Reminders: render the injected REMINDERS block verbatim, preserving each issue as a single clickable markdown-link line (`- [DEV-338 · 53d · Techy Things · Title](https://...)`). Do not split into an ID line plus a separate raw URL line, do not abbreviate to `[URL]`, and do not omit any link. If it says 'None flagged' (e.g. token not configured), write 'None flagged' and never invent time-sensitive items.
ATTENDANCE MODE: every line ends with exactly one of "(online)", "(in person · <place>)", or "(format unknown)". The scraped base lines already carry this — reproduce it verbatim, never drop it and never re-label it. For web-added events, use the same three states: if the page says online/virtual/webinar/Zoom, write "(online)"; if it names a city or venue, write "(in person · <place>)"; if it says neither, write "(format unknown)". Never guess a mode or a city that is not on the page.
- AI Infra Events: reproduce the injected UPCOMING lines verbatim, plus the web-step lines exactly as fetched this run. Never add an event, vendor, date, URL, or attendance mode that was not observed this run — no plausible-looking stand-ins, no invented meeting links. If the block reports a source unavailable or no events in window, say exactly that.
- Links: every URL you emit MUST be inside markdown link syntax or angle brackets. Never emit a bare URL — Discord renders a preview image for every bare one, which floods the channel.

Output format:

**Weather & Reminders**
*   **Weather (Cambridge, VT):** <Now>. <Today>. <Tomorrow> - from the injected context only; never invent or generalize a forecast
*   **Reminders:** <stale open Linear issues, each as a single clickable markdown-link line (- [DEV-338 · 53d · Techy Things · Title](https://...)); or "None flagged">

### AI Infra Events
- One line per event, chronological, earliest first: the injected UPCOMING lines verbatim, plus any BrightTalk/vLLM events found via the web tools. If nothing at all was found, write "event watch unavailable".

### Work Priorities
- Current focus areas only, drawn from the profile. No completion claims.

### Issues / Blockers
- Red-cross items from the scan only
- Anything needing attention, or "Nothing blocking."

Keep it concise. No fluff. Direct format.

jobs.name: Brief - Midday
jobs.prompt:
Produce a polished Midday Check. This is a DELTA report: compare against the morning brief's output and the injected brief context, and report only what changed.

The measured brief context (weather, infra scan, reminders) is injected above under the "===== BRIEF CONTEXT =====" header. Treat that as your ONLY source.

HARD RULES
- Weather: this brief does NOT report weather. Do not include a weather section, a weather delta, or any temperature, humidity, or forecast figure. The 6am and 3pm briefs carry weather.
- Linear Backlog: report the STALE SUMMARY line verbatim (count, average age, delta) followed by every stale issue as a clickable markdown-link line. Never compute, round, or invent these numbers yourself and never state a delta the summary line does not contain.
- Do NOT claim that no work was completed. You cannot observe that. If nothing changed in the injected context, write "No change detected".
- Infra: only red-cross items are issues. "Known-inactive by design" entries are not issues.
- New Stale Issues: list only issues that are in the injected REMINDERS block but were NOT in the morning brief, as single clickable markdown-link lines. If every injected issue was already in the morning brief, write "No new stale issues" and list nothing.

Output format:

Linear Backlog
- Open with the STALE SUMMARY line from the injected REMINDERS block, verbatim: the count, the average age, and the delta line. If it says "No prior baseline on disk", report only the count and average and write no delta.
- Then list every stale issue as a single clickable markdown-link line (`- [DEV-338 · 58d · Techy Things · Title](https://...)`), verbatim. Do not drop, re-sort, or re-label them.

New Stale Issues
- Only issues absent from the morning brief's list, as clickable markdown-link lines. Or "No new stale issues".

Work Status
- Focus areas unchanged, or a change visible in the injected context. No completion claims.

Issues / New Blockers
- New red-cross items; resolution status on earlier flags. If a red-cross was already reported earlier today and its status is unchanged, do not repeat it.

Keep it short. No recap of unchanged items.

jobs.name: Brief - Evening
jobs.prompt:
Produce a polished End-of-Day Wrap. Compare against the day's earlier briefs and the injected brief context.

The measured brief context (weather, infra scan) is injected above under the "===== BRIEF CONTEXT =====" header. Treat that as your ONLY source.

HARD RULES
- Weather: report only values present in the injected context. If it says WEATHER SOURCE UNAVAILABLE, say the outlook is unavailable. Never invent.
- Do NOT state what shipped or did not ship. You cannot observe that. Report only what changed in the injected context.
- Infra: only red-cross items are issues. "Known-inactive by design" entries are not issues.

Output format:

Weather Today
- Final conditions, from the injected context

Day Summary
- What changed on the machine, per the injected context

Open Items Carried to Tomorrow
- If the injected REMINDERS block lists stale issues, surface them under this heading as single clickable markdown-link lines (`- [DEV-338 · 53d · Techy Things · Title](https://...)`), verbatim and one per line. Do not nest them as a continuation of the Day Summary weather bullet, split into an ID line plus a separate raw URL line, abbreviate to `[URL]`, or omit links. If there are none, write "None carried".

Issues / Carry-forwards
- Red-cross items and port changes since morning. If a red-cross was already reported in an earlier brief today and its status is unchanged, do not repeat it.
- Recommended first actions

Keep it tight. One-line verdicts preferred. No fluff.

jobs.name: Gmail Daily Triage
jobs.prompt:
Run email triage on the Gmail inbox. This is a self-contained script execution.

1. Set PATH and GMAIL_APP_PASSWORD: `export PATH="/opt/homebrew/bin:$PATH"` and `export GMAIL_APP_PASSWORD="$(grep '^GMAIL_APP_PASSWORD=' ~/.hermes/.env | cut -d= -f2- | tr -d '"')"` (from ~/.hermes/.env)

2. Run with limit 10: `EMAIL_TRIAGE_LIMIT=10 python3 ~/.hermes/skills/email/email-triage-agent/scripts/triage.py run`

3. After it finishes, review the staged drafts with `python3 ~/.hermes/skills/email/email-triage-agent/scripts/triage.py review`.

4. Report per the OUTPUT FORMAT below. Do NOT send anything — just triage and stage.

PATH FACTS — state these verbatim, never paraphrase or invent:
- Staged drafts live in ~/.hermes/email-drafts (i.e. /Users/macstudio/.hermes/email-drafts). That is the ONLY draft directory. Never cite any other path for drafts. A path like "email-draft-s" is wrong.
- Copy file paths into the report exactly as the script prints them. If the script did not print a path, do not state one.

STAGING SEMANTICS:
- Only action, reply and urgent-reply threads are staged as draft files. noise, reference and waiting threads are appended to classified.log and are NOT staged.
- Report the staged draft count the script prints, not the number of threads processed. Do not describe a logged thread as staged.
- If the script's staged count and the number of files on disk disagree, say so explicitly rather than picking one.

CLASSIFICATION HYGIENE:
- For any thread classified action, reply, or urgent-reply, read the message body before reporting what it asks for. Say explicitly whether the staged draft is safe to send.
- Never report that an email needs a reply if its body says the inbox is unmonitored / "do not reply", or if the sender is automated. Report it as a false positive and recommend discarding it.

OUTPUT FORMAT — follow this shape exactly. Target 15 lines or fewer.

ALWAYS DELIVER A REPORT. Never respond `[SILENT]` and never stay quiet. This is a daily
digest: "nothing new" is a result worth stating, not a reason to say nothing. If no new
drafts staged and no errors, emit the header plus `Nothing new since yesterday.` and stop.

The delivery target is Discord. Markdown tables DO NOT render there — never emit a table. No `====` banner rules. No invented headers beyond the ones below.

📧 **Email triage** — <date>

Processed <N> · staged <S> · errors <E>

**Needs you** (omit the whole block if nothing needs you):
- 🟡 <id> · <sender> — <subject>
  <one line: what it asks for, and whether the draft is safe to send>
- 🔴 same shape, for anything time-sensitive

**False positives** (omit if none):
- <id> · <sender> — <why it is not actionable>
  `triage.py discard <id> <id>`

Nothing sent. Queue: ~/.hermes/email-drafts

RULES FOR THE ABOVE:
- One line per draft. Subject truncated to ~50 chars. No paragraph per draft.
- Confidence scores are noise — never report them.
- Never repeat the run's raw script output or echo its log lines.
- Put the recommendation to discard inside a `triage.py discard <ids>` code span, on ONE line for all false positives. Do not spell out the full absolute path in the report body.
- Do not restate these instructions or describe what you checked. Report the result only.

jobs.name: Hermes Release Watch
jobs.prompt: Release-gate for hermes-agent. no_agent=True: the script IS the job and its stdout is delivered verbatim (empty stdout = silent). Polls api.github.com/repos/NousResearch/hermes-agent/releases/latest anonymously (no token read or sent) and pages ONLY when a new published release tag appears — roughly weekly, versus main's continuous ~1600 commits. exit 0 = silent, exit 1 + stdout = deliver. First run seeded silently at v2026.9.24 so installing the watch never pages. A network or API failure exits 0 silently and is recorded to ~/.hermes/state/hermes-release-watch/last_check.json rather than paging — 'could not check' is not a release. State written BEFORE delivery so a delivery failure cannot double-page. It never writes config.yaml and never runs 'hermes update'; it observes and reports, you decide when to take it. Inspect: hermes-release-watch.py --status | --test-alert | --accept TAG | --reset. NOTE: this gate only watches releases; it does NOT suppress the passive 'N commits behind' banner — 'hermes config set updates.check false' is a separate decision.
